name: Calcium polystyrene sulfonate
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: Hyperkalemia in acute or chronic kidney insufficiency, including dialysis (oral)
usual_adult_dose.dose: 15 g three or four times daily (Calcium Resonium); some products use 20 g 1 to 3 times daily; stop when potassium falls to 5 mmol/L
30 g in 150 mL water or 10% dextrose (Calcium Resonium); some products use 40 g

key_interactions.action: Separate by at least 3 hours (6 hours with gastroparesis).

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Aluminum or magnesium hydroxide, calcium carbonate
key_interactions.action: Separate doses by at least 3 hours.

key_interactions.effect: Toxicity if hypokalemia or hypercalcemia develops.

contraindications: Obstructive bowel disease or reduced gut motility; risk of colonic necrosis
monitoring: Separate from all other oral medicines by at least 3 hours (6 hours with gastroparesis)
Bowel habit (constipation); colonic necrosis can occur even without sorbitol

pk.bioavailability: Not absorbed (calcium released is partly absorbed)
pk.excretion_renal_pct: None; excreted in feces with bound potassium

sources.citation: Aventis Pharma Limited (Sanofi). (2024). Calcium Resonium 99.934% w/w powder for oral/rectal suspension (calcium polystyrene sulfonate) [Summary of product characteristics; text revised January 11, 2024]. Electronic Medicines Compendium (UK).

Fresenius Medical Care Nephrologica Deutschland GmbH. (2007). Sorbisterit powder for oral/rectal suspension (calcium polystyrene sulfonate) [Summary of product characteristics, licence PA1350/002/001; text revised not stated (printed December 2007)]. Health Products Regulatory Authority (Ireland).

Harel, Z., Harel, S., Shah, P. S., Wald, R., Perl, J., & Bell, C. M. (2013). Gastrointestinal adverse events with sodium polystyrene sulfonate (Kayexalate) use: A systematic review. The American Journal of Medicine, 126(3), 264.e9–264.e24.

revision_log.change: Primary source switched to Calcium Resonium SmPC (2024): 15 g three or four times daily, rectal 30 g; 20 g products noted; stop at potassium 5 mmol/L.
Separate all oral medicines by ≥3 h (6 h in gastroparesis); weekly calcium; new interaction row (Calcium Resonium SmPC 4.2, 4.4).
